title: Phased Deprecation & Adapter Policy for Runtime Surface
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: We need a clear, operational policy that allows the runtime team to introduce breaking or behavioral changes with predictable customer impact, automated migration support, and LTS-respecting timelines. Existing semver guidance is broad; this ticket defines a phased deprecation + adapter approach that minimizes large migrations and enables automated client-side mitigation.

Scope: runtime HTTP/gRPC surfaces (requests, response schema, headers), public SDK behavior, and server-side plugin contracts. Not covering internal-only APIs, but includes the Accept-Version/Deprecated headers and rollout automation that touches the control plane.

High-level policy summary: 1) Classify changes as Non-breaking / Minor behavioral / Breaking. 2) For any change that may cause client observable regressions, require a phased-deprecation path: immediate runtime fallback, a generated adapter shim where feasible, telemetry gating, and a clear calendar for LTS vs stable channels. 3) Automation: generate adapter shims (server-side and SDK warnings), expose migration hints in response headers, and provide an amcli migration-assistant that can scan call patterns and recommend flags or pinning. 4) Rollout gates: feature-flagged canary, telemetry-driven canary thresholds, automated rollback triggers, and staged expansion across customer cohorts and Dedicated/Private channels.

Key definitions used in the policy: - Stable channel: default hosted API for most customers; 60-day deprecation window for minor behavioral changes, 180-day for breaking changes with adapter availability. - LTS channel: long-term supported runtime branches (customers can opt-in). Breaking changes require a 360-day notification and at least one supported adapter shim if feasible. - Adapter shim: lightweight translation layer that converts old request/response shapes to new surface or emulates removed behavior for a configurable window. - Breaking change: any change that will cause existing SDKs or production requests to alter correctness or fail unless consumer changes code or pins a version.

Non-goals: forcing every change to be non-breaking, or eliminating all runtime optimizations that require API shifts. We accept that some changes will be disruptive but must follow the policy for customer communication and tooling to mitigate impact.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc with classification table and timelines merged into the release-engineering handbook
Adapter shim generator prototype included in runtime repository and usable for at least two change-types (request rename, response field removal)
amcli migration-assistant prototype that can scan a recorded trace and produce a recommended pin or adapter flag
Rollout gate automation added to the canary pipeline with telemetry thresholds and automated rollback rule configured
Documentation pages and SDK warning header behavior implemented and validated in integration tests
tasks: Draft formal policy text and sample timelines for Stable vs LTS channels
Design adapter shim interface and mapping DSL (RFC + examples)
Implement shim generator for HTTP JSON contract changes (PR + integration tests)
Add Accept-Version and Deprecation-Info response headers and standardize migration hint format
Extend canary pipeline to evaluate error-rate, latency, and correctness signals; add automatic rollback hook
Build amcli migration-assistant to analyze traces and create recommended pin/adapt commands
Run internal dogfooding with 3 product teams to validate migration UX and calendar
Update runtime SDKs to emit deprecation warnings and to surface pinning helpers
